items.summary: Governance near a plausible critical transition faces a resource problem in addition to problems of diagnosis, intervention, and evidence. Elevated susceptibility can increase the value of observation, bounded experimentation, and revisability, while waiting can simultaneously consume the fiscal, material, organizational, temporal, and relational capacities required for survival and later action. This paper develops a discussion framework for that tension. Its central object is functional resource distribution: the allocation of heterogeneous capacities across observation, probing, short-horizon survival, selective commitment, reserve or option preservation, and recovery or repair. The categories are analytical functions rather than a scalar budget partition and can overlap in practice. The paper introduces distributed optionality as a relational property of a response architecture in which materially different future actions remain supported by functionally diverse and sufficiently non-coincident pathways. It distinguishes exact reversal from recoverability, spatial dispersion from independence of failure modes, and delay as information gathering from delay as resource dissipation. The framework inherits, rather than restates, earlier arguments about response-oriented governance and evidence-to-action instability near criticality. Its distinctive question is how governance capacity may be composed when the future regime is uncertain, resources are partly non-substitutable, and both premature commitment and indefinite waiting can narrow the feasible future. The proposal is conditional and non-prescriptive: criticality requires domain-specific empirical support, and the appropriate resource portfolio depends on transition mechanism, horizon, institutional structure, and explicit normative commitments.
items.title: Governance and Survival near Criticality: Functional Resource Distribution and Distributed Optionality

items.summary: Verification and reproducibility code for the revised version of the paper "Closed-form moment propagation through fractional-power response surfaces via the Mellin transform". Reproduces the exact region-of-validity analysis with the mixed-multi-index counterexample, the Mellin transform of the truncated normal, the confluent (log-power) treatment of the degenerate point alpha = 1/2, the 50-digit re-verification of the manufactured-solution benchmark and the separable 2-D propagation, the balanced benchmark over two response classes, the heavy-tail accuracy benchmark, the engineering example (convective cooling under Weibull wind) and the out-of-sample real-data case study on CWRU bearing records 105 and 106 with a moving-block bootstrap. The scripts of the submitted version are kept. Includes the Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the four supporting lemmas.
items.title: Ku-Mellin-PATP: reproducibility code

items.summary: Version 7. A review found that the per-jail table added in version 6 did not match the sentence summarising it, and that it was the one table in the article no script in this deposit produced. Both are fixed. code/analysis/ban_leak_per_jail.py now generates it from the published intervals, prints why its columns do not sum to the across-path table, and marks cells whose denominator is too small to read as a rate. The corrected reading: nine jails are measured under all three paths, the ordering holds inside all nine, iptables-multiport falls to 3.6% or less in seven and to 12.5% in an eighth where that is one leaking interval out of eight, and ipset is zero in eight of the nine, the exception being a single interval in 156. Also added is the method behind a negative claim the article makes, that nothing in the panel's current version writes into its port chain: the search commands, their scope, the files that match, and what a textual search cannot establish. The number-checking script that compares the article against this deposit was extended from 37 claims to 44. Version 6. The open question of whether the chain layout is the panel vendor's default was tested on a clean installation of its current release. The precedence is the default: once the firewall module initialises, the panel places its chain above every chain the firewall front end owns. The accepts that complete the failure are not: with ufw active the current version writes ports into ufw instead, and no code in it writes into the panel's port chain. On the observed host those accepts date to January 2026 and were carried forward across upgrades, so the finding reaches hosts upgraded from earlier versions rather than every installation. The article was narrowed accordingly. Version 5. The reproduction now reads the packet counters on the ban rule, which supplies the third source the measurement lacked: in the leaking cell the counter does not move, while in the cells that hold it records 14 to 17 packets discarded during the same ten probes. The environment is recorded with it. Added too are the creation dates of the panel's port rules, taken from the panel's own database, which date the inert period rather than assuming it, and the attack-class composition table that the article no longer prints. Version 4. The controlled reproduction now crosses three placements of the panel's rule with four enforcement paths, including nftables. The ban leaks in one cell of twelve: the panel-like rule inserted at the head of INPUT combined with fail2ban's ufw action. The identical rule appended after the firewall's chains leaks nothing, which identifies precedence rather than the rule as the cause. Added with it is a note recording what was inspected on the production panel, including the file's SHA-256 and three read-only commands with which any operator can check the same thing on their own host; the vendor's code is not redistributed. Version 3 (peer-review round). Three additions answer what review asked for. First, the cause is now demonstrated rather than described: experiments/reproduce_chain_precedence.sh builds the failure from nothing on a disposable host and runs six combinations of chain arrangement and enforcement path; the ban leaks in exactly one of them, the one matching the production configuration. Sanitised INPUT-chain listings from both production servers are included beside it. Second, registration exposure is counted correctly: submissions (POST) are separated from form loads (GET), and the daily series records how many submissions came from an address then inside an active ban interval. Counting submissions only, they rose 32% while the accounts they produced fell 73% and conversion fell from 41.4% to 8.4%; but only 1.2% of them came from a banned address, so the article no longer claims that endpoint isolates the mechanism. Third, DATA-DEFECTS.md lists all eleven data defects with how each surfaced. Version 2 corrects version 1 and adds the measurement
items.title: Bans that never blocked: data and analysis code for measuring silent enforcement failure

items.summary: The increased demand for data-based decision-making has led to a surge in the use of predictive analytics to identify students at risk of academic failure. However, many tertiary institutions still rely mostly on Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) as an indicator of performance. In this study, we analyzed and compared the predictive capability of three supervised machine learning algorithms (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest) to forecast student academic outcomes using demographic, behavioral, and academic attributes. We preprocessed the dataset through missing-value handling, feature encoding, and scaling, then split it into 70% training and 30% testing sets. We trained, hyperparameter-tuned, and evaluated the models using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC, along with Pearson correlation analysis. Results showed that Random Forest performed best (accuracy 85%, AUC-ROC 0.92), outperforming Logistic Regression (78% accuracy, AUC-ROC 0.88) and Decision Tree (74% accuracy, AUC-ROC 0.82). Correlation analysis showed that prior grade was the strongest predictor (r = 0.94), followed by study time, while absences and age showed negligible association; this association is descriptive, not causal. These findings informed the development of Edupredict , a web-based analytics tool that generates real-time probability-of-pass scores from student-level inputs. As a prototype trained entirely on synthetic data, Edupredict demonstrates that such a tool is technically feasible; the reported metrics should be read as evidence that the analytic pipeline works as intended, not as a validated real-world performance, pending future testing on real institutional data.
items.title: Edupredict: A Comparative Data Analytics Framework for Student Academic Performance Prediction Using Machine Learning Algorithms

items.summary: International Environmental Law stands at a crossroad, where its basic ideas and principles are massively coming at odds with the depth and demand of universal environmental catastrophe. Greatly based upon notions of state control, assent, and fragmented international agreement, the discipline has failed to respond to massive environmental degradation and biodiversity failure. The formation of the scientific notion of the ecological boundaries and limits has elevated the constraint by introducing a bunch of environmental thresholds and limits within which the humankind can remain secure. Developed by the Stockholm Resilience Centre, this framework uncovers crucial biodiversity dynamics like the massive ecological destruction, ecological threshold, poor land usage and change, and bio-geochemical cycles and hence introduces a novice standard beyond which the irreparable environmental damage sharply increases and spikes. While this model has gained impeccable speed and admiration among scientific and policy stakeholders, its ethical interpretation and application for international law remains questionable. This paper argues that adopting environmental limits within the scope and ambit of international environmental law calls for a thorough transformation from fragmented governance towards an obligatory structure of earth system governance.
items.title: Planetary Boundaries And International Environmental Law: Towards Earth System Governance

items.summary: Neural receivers for 5G NR are commonly compared against least-squares (LS) baselines, which leaves open whether they improve on a well-tuned classical receiver and whether their gains survive conditions outside the training distribution. We evaluate a fully convolutional neural receiver and a lightweight hybrid receiver, which retains a classical LS and linear minimum mean-squared error (LMMSE) front end and learns a residual correction of its log-likelihood ratios, on standard-compliant 5G NR PUSCH with 3GPP tapped delay line channels and hardware impairments. Baselines include an LMMSE channel estimator supplied with the empirical statistics of each test scenario (genie) and one supplied with a single fixed set of statistics from the training mixture (practical). Inside the training range both learned receivers only match the genie baseline. Two regimes differ. With an RMS delay spread of 2000 ns the learned receivers require 0.90 dB less than the genie baseline, while the practical LMMSE receiver does not reach 10 percent BLER at all; with a single DMRS symbol the neural receiver requires 4.08 dB less than the best classical receiver at 20 m/s and is the only receiver that operates at 30 m/s. We further show that the apparent failure of learned receivers outside the training envelope is a matter of training coverage rather than architecture: widening the training delay spread from 30-300 ns to 30-1000 ns converts a 5.97 dB deficit at 2000 ns into a 0.90 dB advantage, at a cost of at most 0.1 dB for speeds up to 45 m/s. Trained on the same range, the hybrid receiver matches the full neural receiver within 0.05 dB using 3.9x fewer parameters and FLOPs. Finally, we document a baseline pitfall: DMRS-based carrier frequency offset compensation also removes the Doppler shift of a dominant line-of-sight path, invalidating the LMMSE correlation model and costing 0.84 dB, which can produce illusory gains for learned receivers. Code, configurations and results: https://github.com/Ewwftyy/neural-receiver-5g-nr
items.title: Training Coverage, Not Architecture, Decides When Learned 5G NR Receivers Help

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22967519 . This paper looks at what happens when we trust an AI coding agent's work without independently checking what actually changed. The authors show a case where a protected file was changed, but GTB still returned VERIFIED because the file was left out of the verification process. I thought one of the strongest parts of the paper was the distinction between stopping an agent from doing something and actually being able to prove that it didn't do it . The paper also does a good job of showing the attack in practice, explaining why the verification failed, and suggesting ways to make the process more reliable. Major issues The experiment focuses on GTB, so testing other coding-agent or verification systems would help show whether the issue is specific to GTB or appears more broadly. The proposed fixes have not yet been independently tested. Testing them against the same attack, along with a few variations, would make the results more convincing. Minor issues Including the exact software versions and experimental environment would make the experiment easier to reproduce. A simple diagram showing the normal verification path and where the modified file gets excluded would make the main failure easier to understand. It would also be useful to state how many times the attack was repeated and whether the same result occurred consistently Competing interests The author declares that they have no competing interests. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) The author declares that they did not use generative AI to come up with new ideas for their review.
items.title: PREreview of "Beyond Agent Self-Reporting: Evidence-Based Verification of Autonomous AI Software Work"

items.summary: Pipeline and derived matrices for a three-domain calibration of cross-study agreement among public transcriptomic signatures. The analysis covers 19 human datasets: peripheral blood in COVID-19 (10 datasets), peripheral blood in sepsis (5), and aortic wall in dissection or aneurysm (4). This gives 61 pairwise signature comparisons. Headline results. Median pairwise Jaccard overlap was 0.014, 0.072 and 0.023 across the three domains. Observed overlap was 5.6, 10.2 and 6.5 times the expectation for random gene sets of the same size, with 47 of 61 pairs significant after FDR correction. Consensus across ten COVID-19 blood datasets retained two genes from a union of 4,225, and relaxing agreement to 20 per cent retained 717. Simulations with a known shared 250-gene signature hold at 250 for every k and converge after two datasets, so the failure is unstable detection rather than sample size. The release contains a size-aware concordance measure, a permutation null, consensus analysis across datasets, ground-truth simulations in shared-signal and private-signal regimes, and an offline reproduction bundle. No expression matrices are redistributed; all 19 datasets are public and cited by accession in the paper.
items.title: Size-aware cross-dataset concordance of public transcriptomic signatures

items.summary: Conventional black-box predictive models consistently exhaust the limited memory boundaries of industrial edge microcontrollers. Massive parameter footprints and opaque decision pathways render standard neural networks highly vulnerable to out-of-distribution catastrophic failures. The proposed physics-informed symbolic artificial intelligence architecture formulates transparent degradation equations tailored directly to individual hardware characteristics. An autonomous generator fuses fundamental electrical constraints with a localized polynomial expansion to produce extreme low-dimensional operational logic. Empirical evaluations utilizing the NASA Ames repository demonstrate the absolute elimination of cross-run extrapolation errors. The customized equations require a strict maximum footprint of 140 Bytes and execute at a constant O(1) inference complexity. The explicit physical formulation reduces total execution energy consumption by a factor of 2.8 compared to baseline multi-layer perceptrons, while maintaining a 0.9994 accuracy score under severe data scarcity. Synthetic noise injection tests confirm supreme operational resilience against severe sensor distortions. Absolute white-box interpretability provides field engineers with the direct capability to audit the precise prognostic logic prior to chip deployment. The decentralized deployment of deterministic diagnostic intelligence establishes a highly robust foundation for sustainable smart manufacturing ecosystems.
items.title: Physics-Informed Symbolic AI: An Explainable Edge-Native Framework for Industrial Prognostics

items.summary: The clinical laboratory diagnostic service is the backbone of all medical decisions, but at the health sector the results of laboratory tests for patients are becoming conflicted between various health care sectors in many regions including Kirkuk, Iraq.This diagnostic mismatch jeopardizes timely medical care, imposes a financial burden on twice on patients and significantly undermines public trust of the local health system. This study explores the causes of intra- and inter-laboratory differences, which span the diagnostic testing experience and can be broken down into pre-analytical (60-70% of errors), analytical (10-15%) and post-analytical (15-20%) phases. These inconsistencies undermine patients' trust in healthcare providers and institutions, leading them to view such issues as evidence of systemic healthcare failures. The study identifies and outlines targeted mitigation strategies through analysis of patient preparation, specimen collection and instrument calibration, and data transcription. Solving this health-care problem needs two strategies: First, laboratory staff must follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) with great care, as well as strictly follow the sample rejection criteria, and apply Internal Quality Control (IQC). Second, structural governance of Directorate of Health is required: mandatory ISO 15189 accreditation, centralized External Quality Assessment (EQA) programs, unannounced audits and agreed upon provincial reference intervals are crucial to recon gain patient confidence and obtain diagnostic reliability.
tags: Laboratory diagnostics, specimen collection, health system.
items.title: Discrepancies in Laboratory Test Results and Their Impact on Patient Confidence in The Health System in Kirkuk, Iraq

items.summary: The verdict, stated first: the universe of the Riemann Hypothesis is closed, its value reached and spent; the hypothesis is not derived on the ladder, and provably not derivable from the register's resources; the last bit is the least-erasure posit, at the grade of the root, refuted by one zero; and the whole route is one kernel term, `RHGround.rh_ground_closure_complete`, on `propext` and `Quot.sound` alone. Part IV is the paper. Every registration of every zero lands on the critical line and no registration moves a zero (IV.1, IV.7); the hypothesis is exactly lossless registration (IV.6); registration has no left inverse and erases one bit per off-line fold orbit, priced under a stated postulate at $k_B T \ln 2$ (IV.4, IV.5); time never moves a zero, and act and being meet only on the line (IV.9 to IV.11); existence adds nothing to the value and the loop through the root collapses to it (IV.12, IV.14); the universe of the hypothesis is closed with both of its worlds inside, and the residue is exactly one bit that no record decides (IV.16, IV.17). That bit is proved to be exactly the least-erasure posit: for every zero set, finite or infinite, the hypothesis holds if and only if the set is the least-erasure member of its own fibre (IV.19, IV.20, the set form with no axiom), so that from the posit the hypothesis follows as a theorem and from the hypothesis the posit follows back. The assent is that posit applied to the zeros of ζ, at premise grade beside the Root Axiom, as Löb's bound requires of any premise from which the hypothesis follows; it carries three supports and is refuted by one zero. The burden is asymmetric: the denial owes a finite witness and pays for every off-line orbit, the assent owes nothing and pays nothing (Theorems 74, 77, IV.19). Parts I to III are the prequel and hand Part IV its three bits. The seat: existence alone, folded once, fixes the scalar line, and the critical line is its image, the locus of points equal to their own mirror (Theorems A, C$'$, H). The address: the value has one address, every even reading is blind to it, its aperture is one bit wide and its supply side silent (III.45 to III.49). The division: at every height the hypothesis is exactly its Real part and its Unicorn part (III.11); the Real part holds to $3 \times 10^{12}$ on the cited certificate (III.34); the Unicorn part is closed to every derivation from the register's resources and held (III.45 to III.49), the fused sentence retired as the wrong unit (III.2, III.3), ZFC placed under RAM as a ladder inside the Ground (III.15 to III.17). Existence decides the seat, does not derive the value (Theorem E, IV.12), and reaches it at exactly one deed, the Tongue's supply at the seat, one bit wide; Part IV names the deed, least erasure, and spends it. Every kernel theorem is checked in core Lean 4.19.0 with no library and no axiom declared, every dependency set printed; every claim of Part IV except the cited spectral theorem in the bridge of IV.8 is executed a second time in Fortran, 13,081 checks and zero failures. Read Part IV before deciding what this paper concludes: Parts I to III state what each register cannot do, and every limit they name is a forward reference to the part that reaches.
items.title: Nothing Escapes, Three Plus One: A Formal Closure of the Riemann Hypothesis. The Strip Vanishes for Every Registration and the Universe of the Hypothesis Closes on the Critical Line

items.summary: Yearbook of the "George Barițiu" Institute of History of Cluj-Napoca, Series HUMANISTICA; Vol. 16 (2018); pp. 249–257. Abstract: The present study aims to make a comparison between the two decisions pronounced in the matter of persons' freedom of movement, more precisely concerning the right of access at the social system of the host Member State, pointing out the fact that, although the situations were similar and the applicable norms were the same (i.e. the Regulation 883/2004 and the Directive 38/2004), the solution of the Court was different, more precisely opposite. So, in the first case, relying only on the Directive, the Court has found out that the European citizens have the right of access at the social systems of the Member States, other than those of citizenship, on the territory of which they have the residence (even though the last is not legal), while in the second case, relying only on the Regulation, it decided that such a right does not exist. It is interesting that, in the second case, the Commission itself relied in its conclusions on the Decision Brey, so waiting for the same solution. Such a turn was not explained by the Court and cannot be explained but politically, by the desire of the Court to convince the Great Britain not to retreat from the European Union. It must be mentioned that the fact that the first decision was pronounced in a preliminary ruling procedure – one which involves a national jurisdiction which has to solve a litigation and, for this purpose, rises to the Union jurisdictions a question of Union law –, while the second in a direct action before the Union jurisdictions, more precisely a procedure against a Member State for failure to fulfil an obligation imposed by the Union law, is not relevant. English title: Comparison between the Decision Brey 140/12 of 19.09.2013 and the Decision Commission/Great Britain 308/14 of 14.06.2016 of the Court of Justice or the European Union in the matter of the free movement of persons (the right of access at the social system of the host State). How to cite: Lazăr, C. (2018). items.summary: We present a novel methodology for trustworthy network intrusion detection in 6G zero‑touch environments by uniting evidential deep learning (EDL) and tabular foundation models (TFM). Two models, a standard MLP and a modern TabICL TFM, are augmented with probabilistic outputs, using either a (frequentist) Dirichlet-based output or an (approximate Bayesian) Monte Carlo dropout (MCD) technique. A post‑hoc uncertainty quantification (UQ) pipeline, comprising the model calibration method and the conformal inference method is then employed to produce reliable uncertainty estimates. The quality of the ensuing uncertainty‑aware outcomes is evaluated using an uncertainty confusion matrix and two key metrics: True Certain Ratio (TCR) and False Certain Ratio (FCR). Extensive testing demonstrates that the anticipated pipeline successfully reduces overconfidence while retaining competitive detection accuracy. Findings indicate a trade‑off between the two key metrics; most important, the UQ pipeline drastically reduces the undoubtedly most dangerous false-certain failure cases. Linear regression is further utilized to assess the influence of various factors on the observed metrics, giving insight into the repeatability and the interpretability of the framework, and inter alia revealing the superiority (or at least the non-inferiority) of the Dirichlet-based output method combined with the TabICLv2 TFM, in terms of trustworthiness.
tags: 6G network intrusion detection, ZSM, trustworthy  AI, evidential deep learning, foundational deep learning, TabICL.
items.title: Combining Evidential and Foundational Deep Learning towards Automated Intrusion Detection for Trustworthy 6G Networks

items.summary: Let a consumer trust its cache instead of re-fetching it trust_cached_entries (default False ) serves a cache entry as it is on disk: no staleness re-fetch, and no full-text retry. Staleness re-fetching suits a cache the tool owns and can rebuild. For a cache that is committed to a repository and reviewed it inverts — the re-fetch becomes the risk rather than the repair. Three failures reported downstream were the same re-fetch seen from different angles: an unstamped full_text_html entry withheld, pointing at a repair route that cannot be reached ( dismech#12672 ) a fetch returning PMC's bot-check page on an HTTP 200, its <title> then compared against the curated title ( dismech#12867 ) a re-fetch shortening 64 bodies and breaking snippets that had verified, in a pull request about something else ( dismech#12879 ) Setting the flag removes the fetch, so there is no window in which any of them can happen. The default is unchanged, so caches still migrate for consumers that want that. The trade is explicit: an imperfect cached entry stays imperfect. That is a content problem to fix deliberately — cache reference --force still rebuilds one on purpose — rather than something re-litigated on every validation run. Also in this release Review follow-ups from #94: a test for the refused-overwrite path that consumers actually take (the previous tests only covered _stale_fallback ), a stale-HTML warning that no longer advises a retry that cannot succeed for a PMC-only article, find_pmc_article_body made public since two modules share it, and a note that PMC_ARTICLE_BODY_CLASSES is ordered by priority. Full changelog: https://github.com/linkml/linkml-reference-validator/compare/v0.3.0rc2...v0.3.0rc3
items.title: linkml/linkml-reference-validator: v0.3.0rc3

items.summary: This paper argues that river deltas and arterial trees, though studied in separate fields, share a common mathematical architecture. Using side-by-side images as a Rosetta stone, it treats their resemblance as a diagnostic clue rather than a metaphor. Both are described as rooted, planar, directed, space-filling trees with a single inlet, repeated branching, and many terminal outlets. At every internal junction, flow is conserved. Both exhibit hierarchical scaling and self-similarity. The central contribution is a common variational template. If a branching network minimizes a separable cost combining transport dissipation and maintenance or volume cost, then optimal branch sizes at each junction obey a power-law relation. The exponent depends on the physics: viscous laminar flow yields Murray's law for blood vessels, while Manning-style open-channel flow yields a different, testable river scaling. Thus the template does not prove identity; it shows that one abstract optimization structure can generate known biological scaling and a conditional geophysical prediction. The paper then asks why such similarity exists. It offers conjectures: convergent optimization, constructal law, diffusion-limited aggregation, resource constraints, robustness, and a universal attractor. It states falsification tests: scaling exponents and graph metrics should not be random after conditioning on constraints, and diagnostics should transfer across domains. A second theoretical part connects the networks to thin and thick chaos. It defines a diagnostic tuple and proves transport-graph invariance: if two transport graphs are isomorphic in the relevant sense, preserving coherent and failure regions and the ordering of edge weights, then thin, transitional, and thick classifications transfer. This supports cross-domain diagnostics for flood forecasting and cardiovascular risk, for example, tracking failure pathways. The paper is careful about limits. Rivers and arteries differ physically in fluid, compliance, timescale, and dynamics. The claim is structural and mathematical, not physical identity. The unity is a shared abstract architecture, not sameness.
items.title: One Tree, Two Fluids: Convergent Mathematical Architecture of River Deltas and Arterial Trees

items.summary: A free lecture series for senior engineering capstone students. It adapts Strauss Zelnick's Success: A Concise Guide to Having the Life You Want (2nd ed., 2015) to engineering careers, alongside Morse, Schell & Babcock's Managing Engineering and Technology (7th ed., 2020). What's inside An introduction: The Control System for Success Nine lectures, from Knowing What You Want to Renewal A conclusion: Closing the Loop The Engineer's Roadmap: the whole series on one page After a Failure: a one-page decision chart Every part includes Its own case study Discussion questions and assignments A glossary and references Distributed free of charge with the permission of Strauss Zelnick; that permission is not an endorsement. Quoted material remains the property of its copyright holders.
items.title: Success as an Engineer: The Complete Series

items.summary: Overview This deposit contains the five input files required to reproduce the Community Terrestrial Systems Model (CTSM) simulations reported in Cheng et al. (2026), which evaluate how Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK)-informed prescribed and cultural burning affects low-flow dynamics and salmonid habitat in the Salmon River watershed of the Klamath River Basin, northern California. The burning targets encoded in these files were co-developed with cultural practitioners and Department of Natural Resources staff of the Karuk Tribe through an iterative co-design process described in the associated paper. They represent aspirational land cover trajectories grounded in Karuk management priorities, not forecasts of expected land cover change. All simulations were run with CTSM in Satellite Phenology (SP) mode at 1-km spatial resolution. Files are in netCDF CDF-5 format ( cdf5 in the file names); readers require a netCDF library built with CDF-5 support. File inventory domain.klamath.ctsm.cropped.230717.cdf5.nc — Domain file defining the 1-km model grid cropped to the study region: grid cell center and vertex coordinates, land fraction, land/ocean mask, and cell area. Shared by all simulations. klamath.optz_params.cdf5.nc — Calibrated CTSM parameter file. Default parameters produced substantial streamflow biases against USGS gage 11522500 (Salmon River); parameters were optimized using Adaptive Surrogate Modeling-based Optimization (ASMO), improving daily Kling-Gupta Efficiency from 0.49 to 0.62. This file supersedes the default CTSM parameter file for all simulations reported in the paper. surfdata_klamath_hist_78pfts_CMIP6_simyr2005_c220513_OM_HRES.NAT_PCT.cdf5.nc — Baseline (historical) surface dataset. Derived from the standard CMIP6 78-PFT surface dataset for simulation year 2005, regridded to the 1-km domain. Natural vegetation is dominated by needleleaf evergreen trees (96.3% of vegetated cover), reflecting a century of industrial timber management. Used in the Baseline experiment (1981–2020) and in all experiments holding land cover at historical conditions. surfdata_..._NAT_PCT.2050.cdf5.nc — Mid-21st century (2050s) burning-scenario surface dataset. Represents a static land cover snapshot under a near-term, planning-constrained burning trajectory built from existing fire management instruments (Western Klamath Restoration Partnership planning areas; Community Wildfire Protection Plans for Happy Camp, Salmon River, Somes Bar, and Orleans).  surfdata_..._NAT_PCT.2100.cdf5.nc — Late-21st century (2100s) burning-scenario surface dataset. Represents basin-wide application of the full TEK-informed spatial zonation (riparian, oak woodland, serpentine meadow, and high-elevation conifer–meadow mosaics organized by distance from river corridors and elevation).  The two scenario surface datasets were generated by modifying the natural-vegetation PFT percentage field (and, by construction, bare-ground fraction) of the baseline file; all other surface properties — soil texture, organic matter content, topographic parameters, and non-vegetated land unit fractions — are inherited unchanged. This isolates the land cover signal in the factorial attribution experiments.

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22979721 . The paper looks at whether we can spot open-source projects that are starting to lose maintainability before the problem becomes obvious. It uses activity and code-quality data from 2,800 GitHub repositories and compares Random Forest, XGBoost, and a Temporal Fusion Transformer. The main finding is that contributor activity and slow PRs seem to give earlier warning signs than code metrics alone. I read this as an empirical software engineering paper rather than a framework advertisement. I like the basic idea of looking at how a project changes over time instead of judging it from one snapshot. My comments are mostly about a few things I would want to understand better before using the framework in practice. The dataset The 2,800 repositories The paper starts with 15,000 repositories and then applies several filters. I would like to see how many repositories remain after each step. That would make it much easier to understand what the final dataset actually contains. The "abandoned" label A project is considered abandoned when its commit activity drops below 20% of its historical peak and it has no merged PRs for four weeks. I think this is an important part of the whole experiment, so I would like to see a few examples of projects that received this label. Four weeks of low activity could mean different things for different projects. The model The 0.84 F1 score The TFT gets an F1 of 0.84 for the six-month prediction task. I wanted to see the Random Forest, XGBoost, and TFT results together, including precision and recall. That would make it easier to understand where the improvement from the TFT is actually coming from. Prediction vs. explanation The models show that contributor distribution and PR resolution time are useful predictors. The discussion then connects this to maintainer burnout and contributors leaving the project. That explanation is interesting, but the experiment mainly shows a predictive relationship. I would separate the model result from the proposed explanation a little more clearly. The code metrics The code-quality measurements The paper uses cyclomatic complexity, code smell density, technical debt, and test coverage as product features. I would like a little more detail on how these measurements were collected across the different programming languages. In particular, it would help to explain which tools were used for each language and how missing measurements were handled. The CPSI score The Composite Project Sustainability Index is presented as something an engineering team could use when checking its dependencies. I think one real repository example would help here: show the CPSI over time and which project metrics caused it to increase or decrease. The practical side The GitHub limitation The dataset focuses on popular GitHub repositories in five programming languages. The authors acknowledge this limitation, but I think it matters when the paper talks about open-source projects more generally. I would make it clearer that the conclusions are based on this particular GitHub sample rather than the whole OSS ecosystem. items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22958187 . The baseline strategy of evaluating clinical sample types to optimize qPCR diagnostic sensitivity grids for Canine Distemper Virus is highly relevant to contemporary mole ular virology. Independent validation of different antemortem matrices is historically neglected, leading to false negatives during acute viral shielding windows. While the comparative approach across urine, conjunctival, and whole blood fractions is structurally useful, the underlying experimental design requires tighter calibration boundaries regarding extraction variance. The authors must fully report the specific standard deviations and intra-assay coefficients of variation observed across high-density Ct values. Bypassing these numerical data limits introduces significant noise into target copy number estimations. Additionally, tracking target sequence mutations that dynamically alter primer-bining kinetics under selective host pressures is essential to prove long-term assay validation. This technical adjustment establishes an objective benchmark for diagnostic networks mapping cross-host morbillivirus transmission tracks without dry-lab limitations. items.summary: DNA barcoding using mitochondrial COI is widely applied for animal species identification, but its accuracy in mammals can be affected by uneven sampling, sequence artefacts, and nuclear mitochondrial pseudogenes (numts). In this study, we established a voucher-linked COI DNA barcode reference library for non-volant terrestrial mammals of Taiwan and evaluated its identification performance and potential limitations using the BOLD workbench, Barcode Index Number (BIN) assignments, barcode gap analyses, and comparisons with public sequence data. A total of 157 newly generated COI sequences were obtained, representing seven orders, 16 families, 37 genera and 48 species. Among the 48 sampled taxa, 15 (31.25%) had no COI barcode record available in BOLD before this study; therefore, the deposition of the present library increasing BOLD coverage for the sampled taxa from 68.8% to 100%. In the original BOLD project dataset, 145 of the 157 sequences were assigned to 49 BINs. To evaluate whether the observed barcode patterns were robust for broader sampling, 75 public Taiwanese mammalian COI sequences were incorporated into an expanded Taiwan dataset of 232 sequences. Barcode-gap and Neighbor-Joining analyses showed that 45 of the 48 taxa retained positive barcode gaps after public sequences were added, supporting the utility of COI barcodes for identifying most non-volant terrestrial mammals in Taiwan. Three taxa, Mogera insularis , M. kanoana , and Petaurista grandis , showed negative barcode gaps and/or split clustering patterns and were therefore highlighted for further investigation. In addition, all three newly generated Rattus tanezumi sequences were flagged as putative numts based on anomalous placement and full-length sequence inspection. Our results further emphasize the importance of integrating specimen traceability, functional sequence checks, comparisons with public data, distance-based analyses, and cautious interpretation of BIN results in mammalian DNA barcoding research.
items.title: Construction of a COI DNA barcode reference library for non-volant terrestrial mammals of Taiwan, with notes on the effects of nuclear mitochondrial pseudogenes (numts) on molecular identification

items.summary: A 10 m wall-to-wall probability surface for transitioning-and-above late-successional condition across Maine forestland, with a matching block-bootstrap standard deviation layer and a training-envelope extrapolation flag. Predictions come from a random forest over the 64 Google AlphaEarth Foundations 2024 satellite embedding bands, fitted on 3,015 FIA plots scored with the v5.1 six-axis late-successional and old-growth instrument at a total score of 4 or above. The mosaicked forestland share is 15.18 percent , which falls inside the independent design-based FIA estimate of 14.66 percent (95 percent interval 13.40 to 15.91, EVALID 232301). The surface passed an eleven-gate acceptance suite spanning location, value range, total magnitude and cross-layer consistency, and a separate post-acceptance stress test. Full gate readings, the plot-level spatial agreement test and its permutation null are included. Intended use. This is a continuous probability surface, not a classified map. Ensemble block calibration is attenuated (out-of-fold block slope 0.723 raw, 0.885 disattenuated), which compresses block means toward the middle of the range. Attenuation leaves a state total close to correct but biases a threshold, so a fixed probability cut does not partition the state the way its nominal value implies. Users thresholding this surface should calibrate the cut against design-based estimates for their own domain rather than adopting a nominal value. The fitted random forest and its 20-model block-bootstrap ensemble are included so the surface can be regenerated and audited. Before depositing them, the forest was measured for memorisation of individual training plots: it was fitted with a minimum of 3 samples per leaf, it contains no singleton leaf across any of its 500 trees, and the median leaf holds 7 training plots, so no leaf's split constraints isolate one plot. That measurement is deposited. No FIA true plot coordinates, per-plot embeddings or per-parcel outputs are included in this deposit.
items.title: Maine transitioning-and-above late-successional forest: 10 m probability surface, bootstrap uncertainty and extrapolation flag (2024 AlphaEarth embeddings)

items.summary: A 10 m wall-to-wall probability surface for the CORE4 structural core late-successional condition across New Brunswick forestland, with a matching block-bootstrap standard deviation layer and a training-envelope extrapolation flag. Predictions come from a random forest over the 64 Google AlphaEarth Foundations 2024 satellite embedding bands and a Hansen v1.12 time-since-disturbance covariate, fitted on the 9,042 plot Configuration D basis of the provincial Continuous Land Inventory as delivered under licence, scored with the CORE4 instrument at three of four comparably measured axes (large tree basal area, maturity on maximum diameter, structural diversity, canopy). The mosaicked forestland share is 10.65 percent (bootstrap percentile interval 10.06 to 11.82 across 20 forests), which falls inside the independent design-based estimate of 9.37 percent (95 percent interval 7.71 to 11.03) on the same licensed frame, with no calibration step. The surface passed an eleven-gate acceptance suite spanning location, value range, total magnitude and cross-layer consistency, a plot-level assembly check against a permutation null, and a separate post-acceptance stress test. Why this replaces the earlier New Brunswick surface. A 16 September 2026 surface trained on labels scored from the public CLI release read about half the licensed rate, because the public tree extract misses about half of the plots the licensed records score as structural core on the same plots. Refitting on the licensed labels with nothing else changed is this deposit. The two surfaces correlate at r = 0.80 over 667 million cells and this one sits above the earlier one on 95 percent of them. Intended use. This is a continuous probability surface, not a classified map. Out-of-fold block calibration is attenuated (predicted-on-observed slope 0.262, interval 0.062 to 0.438), which compresses block means toward the middle of the range, leaves the provincial total close to correct and biases a fixed threshold. Users thresholding this surface should calibrate the cut against a design-based estimate for their own domain rather than adopting a nominal value. Ensemble SD rises with probability, so the uncertainty layer is the instrument for reading the high end. The fitted random forest and its 20-model block-bootstrap ensemble are included so the surface can be regenerated and audited; a memorisation measurement on the forest is deposited with them. No plot-level inventory records, plot coordinates, per-plot embeddings, per-holder or per-parcel outputs are included in this deposit. Release of this aggregate product from the licensed inventory was permitted by the New Brunswick partners in September 2026.
items.title: New Brunswick CORE4 structural core late-successional forest: 10 m probability surface, bootstrap uncertainty and extrapolation flag, trained on the licensed provincial inventory (2024 AlphaEarth embeddings)
